# EuropeDoor — design and engineering audit

**Generated by inspection, not recollection.** Every number below was measured
by running a command against this repository on the date of the commit that
carries this file. Nothing here is inferred from a specification.

Where a claim is not measured it is labelled: **MEASURED**, **OBSERVED**,
**INFERRED**, **PROPOSED**.

---

## Part 1 — What was inspected, and what it contained

| # | area | how it was inspected | what was found |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Route architecture | `find site -name '*.html'`, grouped by path depth | 1,072 pages. 891 under `/europe/*` in five nesting levels (50 countries → 130 regions → 319 destinations → 255 places → 137 facets); 40 experience categories, 17 journeys, 17 interests, 13 themes, 12 each of fund/events/motions, 9 stories, 9 discover facets |
| 2 | Page families | route grouping + `pages.py` entry points | Six families: atlas (nested), index pages, editorial, planner/tools, policy, API |
| 3 | Shared shell | `render.page()` signature | ONE function emits `<html>`. Parameters: `world`, `accent`, `wide`, `scripts`, `ld_blocks`, `og`. Both `world` and `accent` raise `ValueError` on an unknown value rather than silently defaulting |
| 4 | CSS and tokens | grep of `assets/css/europedoor.css` | 1,264 lines, one stylesheet, 56 `:root` tokens, 448 custom-property references, 11 type-scale steps, 6 media breakpoints |
| 5 | Primitives | substring count across all 1,072 built pages | masthead/kicker/footer 100%, pagehead 99.9%, crumbs 99.8%, row 91.0%, note 81.2%, card 78.5%, plate 77.8%, band 76.3%, facts 73.1%, btn 57.6%, chip 51.7%, grid 22.6% |
| 6 | JS applications | line count + `fetch(` + `localStorage` per file | planner 1,721L, map 643L, my-europe 394L (8 storage calls), search 385L, discover 270L, events 36L (no fetch, no storage) |
| 7 | Data/index | `data.load()` keys, `site/api/` | 14 data domains; 5 published endpoints (atlas, countries, journeys, search, graph) + geo |
| 8 | Visual generation | `plate-variation.py` | 7 motif families, 319 plates, twin pairs: skyline 3, peaks 32, coast 25, tower 27, isles 5, forest 3, plain 3 |
| 9 | Responsive | browser suite assertions | zero horizontal overflow asserted at 390px on every page shape |
| 10 | Checks | ran all nine gates | 35 static checks / 116,778 things · 652 browser checks · 1,313 section assertions · 358 UX assertions · 22 invariants · 7 motif families |
| 11 | Content | `content-report.py` | 50 countries, 130 regions, 319 destinations, 255 places, 197 experiences, 17 journeys, 9 stories, 8 business records |
| 12 | Performance/security | file sizes, CSP string, `render.HEADERS` | 21.0 MB of HTML across 1,072 pages, mean 19 KB. `default-src 'none'`, six security headers, zero `<img>`, zero inline styles |

---

## Part 2 — Two defects found during this audit

### D1 — The homepage is 2.6× heavier than it was two commits ago. I caused it.

**MEASURED.**

```
site/index.html            118,935 bytes
  hero coastline <svg>      90,133 bytes   (76% of the page)
  8 tile plates + 3 journey plates ~19,000 bytes
```

The previous commit cut the homepage from eight bands to three and reported
**45,806 bytes** as evidence of the restraint. The same commit added the
landmass under the hero dots — correctly, the map was a scatter plot — and
inlined `europe-lod1.json` to do it. The page ended at 118,935 bytes. **I
reported the 45,806 figure and did not re-measure after the map change**, so a
2.6× regression on the single most important page in the product shipped
inside a commit whose stated subject was making that page lighter.

`data/geo/europe-lod0.json` is 30,337 bytes against lod1's 88,505. The hero is
a decorative figure roughly 600 px wide; **INFERRED**, it does not need lod1.

The same geometry is inlined on **51 pages totalling 2.1 MB** — every country
page plus the homepage. Russia 103 KB, Norway and Sweden 75 KB each.

### D2 — Nothing in the check suite measures bytes.

**MEASURED.** The invariant register holds 22 rows. Not one is a page weight,
a payload size or an asset budget:

```
css.breakpoints  css.font_families  css.font_sizes  css.font_weights
css.gold  css.line_heights  css.shadows  css.stylesheets  css.webfonts
js.applications  js.enhancements  plates.motifs_declared
plates.motifs_reachable  primitives.reach  routes.count  routes.hash
safety.img_tags  safety.inline_style_blocks  safety.inline_styles
shell.count  shell.footers_per_page  shell.mastheads_per_page
```

This is why D1 passed 35 static checks, 652 browser checks, 1,313 section
assertions, 358 UX assertions and 22 invariants without a murmur. **The suite
is excellent at structure, semantics, contrast, geometry, licensing and
honesty, and completely blind to size.** Zero webfonts and zero `<img>` tags
are guarded; a 90 KB inline SVG is not.

### D3 — A documentation claim that the register contradicts

**MEASURED.** `CLAUDE.md` line 226 states "Five applications, **two**
enhancements". `docs/invariants.json` — recomputed from the actual JavaScript
on every build — records `js.enhancements: 1`. The measured value is right and
the prose is stale. One is derived, one was typed.

---

## Part 3 — The fifteen questions

### 1. What is already excellent?

**MEASURED, all of it.**

- **The anti-drift architecture.** One shell, one stylesheet, one URL module,
  one projection, one plate geometry feeding two renderers. `render.page()`
  raises on an unknown world rather than defaulting. This is the reason a
  1,072-page site has no divergent mastheads.
- **The check suite as a design instrument.** 22 invariants with a mandatory
  `why` per row; `routes.hash` pinning the URL set through a restyle;
  `docs/palette.json` recomputing every contrast ratio from hexes rather than
  trusting a claim. It has caught its own authors repeatedly.
- **The honesty enforcement.** Seventeen schema refusals (`rating`,
  `review_count`, `featured`, `sponsored`, `price_level`, …), enforced twice —
  in the schema and again at file level. JSON-LD refuses `aggregateRating` and
  refuses present-but-empty properties. The Fund is guarded against its own
  well-meaning maintainers.
- **The licensing discipline.** `fetch.py` refuses to open a socket for a
  source with no licence file. Eurostat NUTS and OpenStreetMap are blocked by
  name, with reasons.
- **The security posture.** `default-src 'none'` with no `'unsafe-inline'`
  anywhere, achieved by *design* — inert JSON data blocks and utility classes
  instead of style attributes — not by exception lists.
- **The derived graph.** 3,716 edges, none stored, `weight` refused except as
  real kilometres.

### 2. What is merely adequate?

- **The plate system.** **MEASURED**: it works, it is deterministic, it is
  reachable, and it now has a variation ceiling. But `mean d` of 0.12–0.25
  across families means a reader scanning a grid sees a *family* before they
  see a *place*. It is a competent generative system, not yet a visual
  signature.
- **Typography.** 11 type steps under a ceiling of 13, system stacks, one
  measure. Disciplined — but discipline is not the same as distinction, and
  the type is currently doing none of the "premium because of typography" work
  §6 of the brief asks for.
- **The interest taxonomy as navigation.** 17 tags, `festivals` has 3 cities
  and `rail` has 11. **OBSERVED**: a tag with three members is a filter that
  will disappoint whoever taps it.
- **`/map` at 440 KB and `/beyond-the-obvious` at 240 KB.** Functional, unbudgeted.

### 3. What is holding EuropeDoor back from flagship quality?

**Not the design system. The content depth.** MEASURED against the
specification's own MVP targets:

| | now | MVP target | |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Places | 255 | 1,000 | 26% |
| Experiences | 197 | 300 | 66% |
| Journeys | 17 | 50 | 34% |
| Stories | 9 | 100 | **9%** |
| Photographs licensed | 0 | — | — |
| Countries fact-checked | 0 of 50 | 50 | **0%** |

**98 destinations have neither a place nor an experience. 34 countries have no
places at all.** A flagship travel product is judged on what a reader finds
when they arrive somewhere specific, and for roughly a third of this atlas the
answer is a summary and a generated plate. No amount of visual work changes
that. **This is the single largest gap between the current state and the
stated standard, and it is editorial, not technical.**

Second: **0 of 50 countries have been fact-checked**, on a site publishing
country facts with a verification-expiry model already built to track it.

### 4. Which changes have the highest visual leverage?

**PROPOSED**, ranked by (visible improvement ÷ risk):

1. **Fix D1 and add a weight invariant.** Highest leverage available: restores
   the flagship page and closes the blind spot that hid it.
2. **The destination page.** 319 of them; it is where a reader lands from
   search and where the product is actually judged. It has had no dedicated
   design pass in this session's record.
3. **Typographic scale at the top end.** One measured change — the display
   size and its measure on `h1` — affects 1,072 pages and is the cheapest
   route to "expensive because of typography".
4. **Plate legibility at card size**, not plate *variety*. The variation work
   is done; the open question is whether a plate reads as *this place* at
   160×100.
5. Everything else is smaller than these four.

### 5. Which changes should NOT be made?

- **Do not add star ratings, review counts or "popular" rankings.** We hold
  zero of them; `checks.py` refuses them in seventeen places. The benchmark
  comp showing "4.9 (2.3k)" cannot be built without inventing data.
- **Do not buy photography yet.** §17 and the repo's own rule: the generated
  system is not exhausted, and its last two experiments each cost nothing and
  found something.
- **Do not introduce Postgres, a server, auth or a framework.** No trigger has
  fired. Static generation currently serves 1,072 pages at a mean of 19 KB.
- **Do not add a `ResultCard` or any new primitive.** No shape has repeated
  three times.
- **Do not expand the type scale to match a mockup's fashion.**
- **Do not restyle in a way that moves a route.** `routes.hash` is the control.

### 6. What can be improved without adding infrastructure?

Everything in Q4. **MEASURED**: the entire product is 17,696 lines of Python
and JavaScript with zero runtime dependencies; the constraint on quality here
is judgement and editorial hours, not capability.

### 7. What should the homepage become?

**It already is what §16 asks for**, as of the previous commit: hero → find
your kind of Europe → journeys → stop, with two `<h2>` bands asserted as both
floor and ceiling. **It needs one fix, not a redesign: D1.**

The competing benchmark comp — a five-section homepage with popularity
rankings, star ratings, an "AI-powered" trust bar and a feature strip — is
**refused** on four separate grounds already recorded above.

### 8. What should country and destination pages become?

**PROPOSED, pending the measurement in Q15.** The country page inlines 75–103
KB of coastline; that is a weight decision to revisit alongside D1. The
destination page is the highest-traffic template in the product and the
least-examined in this session's record. **It should be audited at 390 px
before anything is designed for it** — the brief's own §20.

### 9. Discover Mode?

**OBSERVED**: 270 lines, fetches one index, hoists the shared constraint into
one line above the results rather than repeating it per card. That behaviour is
right and is recorded as a rule. **No change proposed without a measurement
showing a defect.**

### 10. Planner?

**MEASURED**: 1,721 lines — by a factor of 2.7 the largest application in the
product, and the stated conversion. It runs entirely in the browser and the
browser suite has caught real itinerary defects in it (a €700 fortnight routed
through Switzerland; a 2,500 km final leg). **PROPOSED**: the next planner work
should be a UX audit of its *output* — the itinerary as a document a person
reads — not new inputs.

### 11. Map?

**MEASURED**: 440 KB, the heaviest page in the product, and 643 lines of JS.
It is genuinely good — zero-cost real geography, seven layers, no tile
provider. **PROPOSED**: a payload budget, same instrument as D2.

### 12. My Europe?

**MEASURED**: 394 lines, owns all three storage keys, no server. Correct as
built. **PROPOSED**: nothing until there is evidence anyone is hitting a limit.

### 13. Which visual assets need improvement?

- The hero coastline: **weight**, not appearance (D1).
- Plates at *card* size: legibility, not variation.
- `plain` (n=8) and `forest` (n=13): too small to learn from; leave alone.

### 14. Which existing assets should be preserved?

The plate system and its `plate_shapes()` single source; `MAPPROJ`; the Natural
Earth pipeline with its hashes; `docs/palette.json`; the invariant register;
the eleven primitives; the two-world token mechanism; every licence document.

### 15. What should be measured before implementation?

1. **Page weight per template**, and a budget per family. Nothing measures this.
2. **The destination page at 390 px** — the real information hierarchy, before
   any redesign.
3. **Plate legibility at 160×100**, distinct from plate variation.
4. **Which of the 17 interests are viable as navigation** by member count.
5. **Real render cost of the map page** at 440 KB on a mid-range device —
   currently unknown; bytes are not latency.

---

## Part 4 — Staged plan

Each stage is a controlled experiment per §24: measure, smallest change, test,
attack, measure, keep or revert, document.

| stage | work | gate |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Fix D1: hero uses lod0, or the coastline moves to a cached asset. Re-measure the homepage. | homepage under a stated ceiling |
| **2** | Fix D2: add page-weight invariants — per-template ceilings, starting at today's values so nothing is forced to change, only prevented from growing. Prove each fails. | `invariants.py --check` red on a deliberate 20 KB addition |
| **3** | Fix D3: correct the enhancement count in `CLAUDE.md`. | — |
| **4** | Measure the destination page at 390 px and 1280 px. Report before proposing. | no code |
| **5** | Destination page design pass, smallest first. | full ladder |
| **6** | Plate legibility at card size — a new measurement, distinct from variation. | ceiling, as with variation |
| **7** | The display type step, measured for contrast and measure, then applied. | browser suite |

**Stage 1 is a live regression on the flagship page and should not wait behind
this document.**

Content depth (Q3) runs in parallel and is not a design task: it is editorial
hours against 98 empty destinations, 9 stories and 50 unchecked countries.
